text:
alice-rf: Hey team — after upgrading our CI image and Poetry to 1.4, tests started failing in the Docker build. We get an import error when importing the SDK: 

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/tests/test_client.py", line 3, in <module>
    from redwood import Client
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx'

alice-rf: Minimal repro from our Dockerfile: 
```Dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY pyproject.toml poetry.lock ./
RUN pip install poetry==1.4.0
RUN poetry export -f requirements.txt -o requirements.txt
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
CMD ["pytest"]
```

alice-rf: pyproject excerpt: 
```toml
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.11"
redwood-sdk = { version = "^1.8.0", extras = ["httpx", "aws"] }
```

support-bot: Thanks for the report <@alice-rf> — a ticket has been opened (#SUP-1209). A support engineer will follow up. :gear:

omar-s: Quick thought — Poetry extras are not always exported into requirements.txt unless you pass the extras flag to `poetry export`. Which exact `poetry export` command are you using? Also did you try `poetry install` locally and confirm httpx is present?

alice-rf: I'm using the exact command in the Dockerfile above: `poetry export -f requirements.txt -o requirements.txt` (no extra flags). Locally `poetry install` does install httpx (on my dev machine), but CI installs by exporting and then `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

josh-eng: That explains it — `poetry export` doesn't include optional extras by default. In older CI we relied on `poetry install` (which honors extras in the lock/build) but when exporting to requirements.txt you need to include extras explicitly. For Poetry 1.4 the flag is `--extras` (you can repeat it). Example: 
```
poetry export -f requirements.txt --extras httpx --extras aws -o requirements.txt
```
Or export with all extras: `--all-extras` (if available in your Poetry version).

maria-qa: FWIW another compatible workaround is to let pip install the wheel with extras directly in Docker: 
```
RUN pip install "redwood-sdk[httpx,aws]==1.8.0"
```
But that bypasses your lockfile and might cause drift. Better to include extras when exporting or run `poetry install --no-dev --no-root` in CI if you can.

alice-rf: Thanks — I reran CI with `poetry export -f requirements.txt --extras httpx --extras aws -o requirements.txt` and the image built fine and tests passed. Confirmed `pip list` inside container shows httpx 0.24.0.

omar-s: Great — marking as root-cause: missing extras in requirements export. Two follow-ups: 1) pin the export command in your repo/CI to include extras, 2) consider moving to `poetry export --without-hashes` if pip is creating slow builds (we have notes in the docs).

alice-rf: Will do. Also leaving a note for the team: Poetry 1.4 CLI flags changed slightly vs 1.2, so the old CI recipe silently dropped extras after the upgrade. Learned the hard way. :sweat_smile:

josh-eng: Filing a quick doc PR to add a CI snippet for `poetry export` with extras into our onboarding repo.

alice-rf: Thanks all! :tada:
